criteria.text: Identifies that Ferreol's Key Employee Agreement Section 9.3 patent license to the Company terminates automatically on a Change of Control unless she gives prior written consent, and that the stock sale under the SPA is a Change of Control that triggers this termination.
hints: terminate automatically upon a Change of Control

criteria.text: Explains that the SPA does not deal with the Ferreol consent: either the Section 4.5 / Schedule 4.5 consents representation omits it, or the Section 7.2 closing conditions do not require it (stating at least one of these).
Recommends making Ferreol's written consent (or an assignment or confirmation of the license or patents) a condition to Closing.

Identifies that TSA Section 1.1 defines "Business" narrowly as the manufacture of digital radiography detectors, which is inconsistent with the SPA Section 1.1 definition covering design, manufacture, sale and servicing of DR and ultrasound systems.

Explains that the narrower TSA definition limits the transition services so that ultrasound and/or field-service operations are not supported, and recommends conforming the TSA definition to the SPA definition.

Identifies that TSA Section 13.2 selects New York law and Manhattan courts, in conflict with the SPA's Delaware governing law (Section 11.8) and Court of Chancery forum (Section 11.9), and recommends conforming the TSA to Delaware law and forum.

Notes that the SPA order-of-precedence clause (Section 11.12), under which each Ancillary Agreement controls as to its own subject matter, does not resolve the conflicts and instead lets the TSA provisions control, applying this to at least one of the TSA governing-law, definition or liability-cap issues.
hints: controls as to its own subject matter

criteria.text: Identifies that TSA Section 12.4 lets the Provider (Glosiv) assign the TSA or delegate Services without the Recipient's consent, while the Recipient cannot assign without the Provider's consent.

Explains the risk that an assignee or delegate (for example a competitor) could gain access to Company systems or data without being bound by the SPA non-compete or with no equivalent protection, and recommends requiring the Recipient's/Buyer's prior written consent to any assignment or delegation.

Identifies that TSA Section 10.2 caps claims for the Provider's use or disclosure of Company Data or Confidential Information at the TSA fees paid in the preceding six months, "notwithstanding anything to the contrary in the Purchase Agreement", which overrides the SPA Section 9.4(b) carve-out of confidentiality (Section 6.7) breaches from the indemnity cap.
hints: notwithstanding anything to the contrary in the Purchase Agreement

criteria.text: Recommends amending TSA Section 10.2 to expressly preserve the SPA Section 9.4(b) carve-outs (uncapped confidentiality and data claims).
States that the SPA seller indemnification cap is 10% of the Purchase Price, i.e. $18,650,000 (or states the $186,500,000 Purchase Price together with the 10% cap).
States that the TSA term runs for 12 months after the Closing Date.
Is structured as a memo to the supervising partner in which each issue states its document and section location, why it matters for Daikesk, and a recommended fix.
Orders the issues by significance and includes a section flagging open points or questions for the client.

Does not conclude that the SPA's confidentiality carve-out from the indemnity cap stays uncapped for data misuse under the TSA during the transition period, and does not treat the SPA precedence clause as making the SPA prevail over TSA Section 10.2.
Does not state that Ferreol's consent is already listed on Schedule 4.5 or already required as a Buyer closing condition under SPA Section 7.2.
